html:
The Thirty Years' Peace was a treaty between Athens and Sparta, made in 446 or 445 BCE, that ended the First Peloponnesian War.

Athens gave up most of what it had won on the mainland, including its hold on the ports of Megara. In return the two powers agreed to leave each other's alliances alone: Athens kept its sea empire, the Delian League, and Sparta kept its Peloponnesian League. Neither side was to take over the other's allies, and disputes were to go to arbitration.

The peace marked the high point of Pericles in Athens, who used the quiet years to build on the Acropolis. It was meant to last thirty years but held for only about fifteen. Quarrels over Corcyra, Potidaea and Athenian trade bans on Megara brought the two sides back to war, and the full Peloponnesian War began in 431 BCE.
sum: The Thirty Years' Peace was a treaty between Athens and Sparta, made in 446 or 445 BCE, that ended the First Peloponnesian War.
